Combine lights for a 3D scene

Source: R/lights-3d.R
lights_3d.Rd

mode sets how the light changes a face colour. "multiply" scales the colour by the ambient and diffuse light and "tint" scales its distance from white; both darken every channel, so a shaded fill no longer matches its legend key. The signed modes keep the colour readable against its key (Szafir et al. 2016; Kovesi 2015). Each light gives a level in [-1, 1] from the angle between the normal and the light: 0 at neutral degrees, 1 facing the light and -1 facing away, linear in the cosine on each side (ggcube's ramp_smooth()). The levels are averaged over the lights, weighted by their luminance, and scaled by the material's diffuse strength. A level of 0 leaves the colour unchanged.

Usage

lights_3d(
  ...,
  ambient = 0.35,
  mode = "multiply",
  range = NULL,
  neutral = 45,
  shadow = "#1d2b53",
  highlight = "#fff1d6"
)

Arguments

...

Lights made with light_directional(), light_point(), light_head() or light_hemisphere().

ambient

Nonnegative strength of the uniform ambient light.

mode

Colour operation: "multiply", "tint", "lightness", "tone", "overlay" or "soft".

range

Moves at full shadow and full highlight, c(shadow, highlight) with -1 <= shadow <= 0 <= highlight <= 1: fractions of the way to black and white in OKLab lightness for "lightness", to the tone colours for "tone", blend strengths for "overlay" and "soft". NULL takes c(-0.45, 0.3) for "lightness" and c(-0.6, 0.6) otherwise.

neutral

Angle in degrees, in [0, 180), between the normal and the light at which a signed mode leaves the colour unchanged.

shadow, highlight

Tone colours of "tone".

Value

A lighting configuration for coord_3d(). The backends that take one directional light (the path tracer and the raymarch backend) use the first directional light.

Details

  • "lightness" moves the OKLab lightness (Ottosson 2020) toward black by up to the fraction abs(range[1]) in shadow and toward white by up to range[2] in light, and keeps the hue; where the moved colour leaves the sRGB gamut, its chroma is reduced until it fits (ggcube's tone_lightness()).

  • "tone" moves the colour in OKLab toward shadow or highlight, up to the fractions abs(range).

  • "overlay" and "soft" are matplotlib's LightSource blend modes on the encoded colour, with an intensity of 0.5 + level * abs(range) / 2.

Specular highlights of material_3d() are added on top in every mode. Lightness-monotone palettes such as viridis lose the most under shading; isoluminant or diverging palettes combine best with relief shading. guide_colourbar_3d(), guide_coloursteps_3d(), guide_bins_3d() and guide_legend_3d() show the shaded colours of a key.

References

Szafir, Sarikaya, Gleicher (2016). Lightness constancy in surface visualization. IEEE TVCG 22, 2107-2121. doi:10.1109/TVCG.2015.2500240

Kovesi (2015). Good colour maps: how to design them. https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.03700

Ottosson (2020). A perceptual color space for image processing. https://bottosson.github.io/posts/oklab/

Examples

lights_3d(light_head(), light_hemisphere("lightblue", "brown"), ambient = 0.1)
d <- expand.grid(x = seq(-2, 2, length.out = 25), y = seq(-2, 2, length.out = 25))
d$z <- with(d, exp(-(x^2 + y^2)))
ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z, fill = z)) +
  geom_surface_3d(shading = "smooth", colour = NA) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Spectral") +
  coord_3d(light = lights_3d(light_directional(), mode = "lightness"))
